title: Execution after a halting step
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, $P$ a finite program, and $c$ a configuration consisting of a program counter and an integer-indexed memory of $W$-bit words. If one step from $c$ halts with Boolean verdict $v$, then for every nonnegative integer $t$, executing $P$ from $c$ for $t+1$ steps returns $v$ and leaves the memory unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: One step from c halts with verdict v
